english: Vajra statement. Many other spiritual friends say that the Greater Vehicle is the ordinary mind of awakening, namely compassion distinguished by compassion.[^N-B-001]

notes.problem: The glossary has ordinary mind for sems, but no complete bodhicitta, bodhisattva, sentient-being or snying rje entries. The repeated compassion in this sentence is in the source.
notes.treatment: Use ordinary mind of awakening for bodhicitta, bodhisattva and sentient being for the lexicalized personal compounds, and compassion for snying rje; preserve the repetition. These are local proposals, not additions to the active glossary.

english: Here, the ordinary mind of awakening and compassion are distinct: compassion is present even in hawks and wolves, non-Buddhist outsiders, and Buddhist hearers and solitary realizers. The ordinary mind of awakening does not arise from just one such cause or condition, but from immeasurably many. The Cloud of Jewels says:
Having faith in the victors and the victors’ Dharma,

and so forth. They differ also as cause and result, since [the source says] it is not a result produced by compassion and the rest.[^N-B-002] Their functions differ, since [the ordinary mind of awakening] brings about the attainment of buddhahood; their objects of focus differ, since it focuses on both samsara and nirvana. Thus the claim is merely loose talk that fails to distinguish compassion from great compassion.

notes.problem: The explicit negation seems difficult beside the argument distinguishing cause and result.
notes.treatment: Retain not; do not silently emend to is a result.
notes.uncertainty: The referent of the negative clause remains uncertain.

english: Vajra statement. Others say: “The bodhisattva vow needs no support in individual liberation, because individual liberation [vows] arise only in men and women of the three continents, whereas the ordinary mind of awakening is said to arise in all.”

Here it is maintained that the bodhisattva vow is attained with individual liberation as its support. Like the foundation stones of a castle, it supports the bodhisattva vow in arising where it has not arisen, abiding once arisen, and being enhanced ever further once abiding, until its culmination. Thus Lord Jowo says:
Of the seven classes of individual liberation,
“Always …” and so forth; also:

Just as here a tree’s root is foremost,
Thoroughly increasing …
Likewise, the holy Dharma ×
The Ground and root ✖[^N-B-003]

notes.problem: The quotation is abbreviated and contains explicit × and ✖ placeholders.
notes.treatment: Keep the fragments and marks; do not reconstruct unquoted verse. Capitalization of The Ground provisionally follows the glossary display.
notes.uncertainty: Missing wording and the application of the technical Ground entry in this metaphor need review.
notes.review_action: Identify the quotation and check the original witness; approve contextual ground usage separately.

Vajra statement. Others maintain that the defining characteristic of the ordinary mind of awakening is given in the Ornament of Clear Realization:

Arousing the ordinary mind [of awakening] is desiring
Complete, perfect awakening for the sake of others.

So it says. Its objects of focus are perfect awakening through discerning knowing and sentient beings through compassion—that is, nirvana and samsara. Its companion is aspiration. Its divisions include the “inexhaustible” in terms of companions; four, beginning with Dharma activity, in terms of levels; relative and ultimate in terms of object; aspiration and engagement in terms of essence; subtle and coarse; and the two attainments through signs and through the nature of phenomena.[^N-B-006]

english: In summary there are three: aspiration, engagement, and the ultimate on the first level. Although others hold that the engagement vow arises only after attaining a level, here [the teaching is otherwise]. Candragomin’s Twenty Verses on Vows summarizes the meaning of Engaging in Bodhisattva Activity, the Compendium of Training, and other works that gather the entire bodhisattva scriptural collection:

english: These four root downfalls cannot occur in one on the first level, because that person has abandoned the 112 things abandoned by seeing and is free from the view of the transitory collection. Thus, regarding “I” and “mine” in this way, it is maintained that the engagement vow can arise even in an ordinary person.[^N-B-008]

english: Vajra statement. Others say: “The engagement vow comprises restraint, gathering virtuous qualities, and benefiting sentient beings. Unless all three are accomplished, it is not the engagement vow.” Here, completing all three in their entirety is beyond even a tenth-level bodhisattva, because it belongs to the sphere of buddhas alone.
Although Sudhana’s gurus were on the tenth level, each [knew] only one or two ways of practice; as they said, “How could [we] know the others?”[^N-B-009]

english: Thus aspiration is the ordinary mind that wishes to attain buddhahood; the engagement vow is employing the three doors virtuously for that purpose. By practising whichever one or two things one can, to the extent one is capable, without letting them deteriorate, and accomplishing them under the power of the aspiring ordinary mind, one enters the engagement vow.

Addendum. It is commonly accepted that after attaining the first level there is no fear of the lower destinies. Here, however, not only at the first level: there are bodhisattvas who have attained pure levels yet go to lower destinies when the dependently arising factors of nonvirtue come together. They go when the two—latent obscurations of the knowable as cause, and the condition—come together, because the character of dependent arising does not change.

Examples include the youth Chukye, King Paljin, and bodhisattvas who went into animal births as an ox, a bear, a monkey, and others. Their going is unlike that of other beings. The Ornament of the Sutras says:

All his phenomena are like an illusion …[^N-B-010]
Birth, a pleasure garden …
Times of prosperity and ×
Afflictions …

english: Addendum. The impossibility of falling after seeing the truth on the first level applies when the cause has not been enacted. If the cause is enacted, even one on the tenth level will fall, because buddhas follow causes and conditions. If that is not established, causes and conditions would be denied, leading to the extremes of permanence and annihilation. Therefore, when the cause is enacted, its result cannot be prevented.

Some say: “Of rejecting and accepting in the bodhisattva vow, a fault is afflicted when, for example, one makes an offering to the Jewels through the three poisons; it is unafflicted when one fails to accomplish it through laziness, indolence, and so forth. When one cannot do it owing to conditions such as fever, there is no downfall.”[^N-B-012]

notes.problem: The opening example appears compressed and may lack a negation; the following debate attacks the proposed unafflicted category.
notes.treatment: Retain making the offering as supplied and mark the speaker’s position as a quotation.

notes.review_action: Check the vow-classification passage in its witness.

english: Taking that claim as the subject: if the distinction is fixed as downfall or no downfall, it follows that an unafflicted downfall is impossible, because there is no phenomenon outside virtue and nonvirtue. For example, when everything is included in samsara and nirvana, a third category is impossible.

Again, taking that as the subject, it follows that [a downfall] is nonvirtuous and afflicted, since “downfall” means falling ever lower. Taking what is unafflicted as the subject, it follows that it is not a downfall, since it is free from the cause, affliction—as with a buddha. Taking laziness and the rest as the subject, they are afflicted, because they are root or subsidiary afflictions.
The Continuum of Dakini Vows says:

Not knowing and heedlessness,
Inability and affliction,
Forgetfulness and unclear mindfulness:
These six cause samaya to deteriorate.
Thus an unafflicted downfall is impossible and is not established.

Vajra statement. Others say: “For bodhisattvas, killing and the rest become virtuous for the sake of others and are not faults, as with the captain Great Compassion and the brahmin youth Karma.”[^N-B-013]

notes.problem: The youth’s Tibetan name is skar ma; the reference identifies Jyotipala without source evidence here.
notes.treatment: Retain Tibetan name as Karma, rather than assert a Sanskrit identification.
notes.uncertainty: Identity unresolved.
notes.review_action: Check the cited narrative and proper name.

english: Here there is no permission on the grounds that it does not become a fault. Permission is given to bodhisattvas who have utterly cast themselves aside, attained forbearance for others’ sake, and can abide in hell. The Sutra of the Truth of Pure Magical Display says:

Over the involuntary arising of karmic maturation,
The blessed Buddha does not exercise dominion.

And in the Great Secret of Skillful Means, King Rabchok says: “To generate roots of virtue in one sentient being, such things will arise for beings in the future. To abide in hell for a hundred thousand eons as a consequence is easy; giving up that single being’s roots of virtue is not like that.”[^N-B-014]

english: Vajra statement. Although others maintain that bodhisattvas engage skillfully in nonvirtue, taking that as the subject, it follows that there is no nonvirtue in the activity of skillful means. Virtue gives rise to higher destinies and liberation; nonvirtue gives rise to the sufferings of samsara and lower destinies, so it cannot ripen and liberate sentient beings—just as darkness cannot illuminate. Therefore the activity of skillful means is exclusively virtuous.
Although all knowable things are taught as bodhisattvas’ training, how could they all be things to accept? Poison must be rejected, but without recognizing it one does not know how to reject it.

The Perfection of Discerning Knowing and the Great Secret of Skillful Means say that activity through skillful means is faultless. This refers to those who have attained forbearance concerning arising phenomena and can bear the result.[^N-B-016]

notes.problem: The phrase says arising phenomena, not the familiar non-arising formula; bkod nus pa also requires interpretation.

notes.uncertainty: Neither a missing negative nor the verb sense is authenticated.

english:
All phenomena, following conditions,
Abide at the tip of aspiration.
Whatever aspiration anyone makes,
A corresponding result will be attained.

Thus aspirations are accomplished; if they are accomplished, the host of sufferings and faults may overwhelm one and obstruct good activity. For example, although noble Shariputra was a sixth-level bodhisattva, giving his body before the time was right created the condition for his falling to the hearer’s level.

Therefore, on accumulation and preparation one should arouse a vast intention and, in application, do as much for others as one can accomplish and sustain. From the path of seeing through the seventh level one enters activity; from the eighth one enters vast activity.[^N-B-018] Therefore Engaging in Bodhisattva Activity says:

Do not harm the body that practises the holy Dharma
For the sake of something trifling.
So it teaches. What, then, should one do? When suffering such as illness arises, one must practise bringing it onto the path, as did Maitrakanyaka.[^N-B-019] This is the Dharma Lord’s own practice.

english: Addendum. Others say that to gather the accumulation of means one must give children, a wife, and so forth to sentient beings below, the field of accumulation. Those are deeds of our Teacher, which we cannot accomplish; temporary benefit alone does not lead to buddhahood.

Therefore the extraordinary practice is the inner accumulation, the practice of kusali yoga. Its field is superior because samsara and nirvana are pure; its intention is superior because it accomplishes the two purposes; and its substance is superior because one transforms the cherished body into nectar and offers it inexhaustibly.
When illness and so forth arise, nothing other than this kusali practice of bringing them onto the path is helpful. This, too, is the exceptional means of clearing obstacles.

On the basis of “whoever harms [a bodhisattva] is connected with happiness,” others say that harming bodhisattvas brings one within their awakened activity because it connects one with happiness. Taking that as the subject: the result of the cause, harming a bodhisattva, is not connected with happiness; that would be unreasonable, since an act motivated by hatred is a seed of suffering—like the fruit of a “six” seed.[^N-B-020] The Sutra of Not Abandoning the Buddha likewise says:

When one harbors an ordinary mind of harm toward another,
Giving does not protect, ethical discipline does not protect,
Meditative stability does not protect, nor do offerings to buddhas.

Also, Engaging in Bodhisattva Activity says, “Whoever, toward such a victor’s child …,” and Entering the Middle Way says, “Because, toward the victors’ children …,” and so forth. “Connected with happiness” refers to a particular portion of the result: for the time being [the bodhisattva] does not retaliate, but protects the person with affection.[^N-B-022]

english: Vajra statement. Of the four alternatives for projecting and completing karma, take the claim that the projecting [cause] is virtue or wrongdoing while [the completing factor] is virtue, so that cause and result are different.[^N-B-023] It follows that this is impossible, since primordial knowing of what is possible and impossible sees the results of virtue and nonvirtue arise separately, just as distinct fruits arise from distinct seeds.

notes.problem: The list of causal alternatives is compressed and apparently asymmetric.
notes.treatment: Supply cause and completing factor in brackets, retaining the stated virtue/wrongdoing sequence.
notes.uncertainty: The exact fourfold formulation remains uncertain.
notes.review_action: Compare with a witness; do not harmonize from standard karma classifications.

english: Therefore when the projecting factor is an accumulation of virtue, the completing factor too is virtue. When the projecting factor is nonvirtue, completion too is through nonvirtue. From the two causes, virtue and wrongdoing, happiness and suffering arise as distinct results.

Sunakshatra and Ajatashatru illustrate this: the initial projecting cause was faith and respect; [they also] committed deeds of immediate retribution. As completing results, Sunakshatra is said eventually to attain liberation, while Ajatashatru was afflicted with burning eruptions and, after death, was born briefly in hell.[^N-B-024]

english: Vajra statement. Others maintain that the ordinary mind of awakening is lost through any one of these: abandoning sentient beings in the conceptual mind, not remembering its benefits, not gathering the two accumulations, not striving in training, the four dark qualities, or faults resembling defeat.

Here it is said to be forgotten, not lost. The Sutra of the Deep Absorption that Gathers All Merit says: “This Licchavi Vimala previously aroused the ordinary mind [of awakening] in Krakucchanda’s teaching. Through practising the four dark qualities he has forgotten it until now; but because he aroused that ordinary mind then, I now give him a prediction.” The Heap of Jewels, the Array of Stems, and others likewise speak of forgetting, not losing.

Thus the Extensive Sutra says that this diamondlike ordinary mind cannot be lost through anything except wrong views, likened to sheep and goats.[^N-B-025] Moreover, even the slightest root of virtue generated toward a buddha is not wasted. Through the power of the enduring, stable tathagata essence, it becomes whichever engagement vow is appropriate; therefore its loss is impossible.

notes.problem: The diamond analogy mentions sheep and goats without explaining the relationship.
notes.treatment: Retain the comparison without adding a substance or causal explanation.
notes.uncertainty: Possibly abbreviated traditional comparison.
notes.review_action: Verify the complete scriptural simile.

english: Vajra statement. Others say that the three obscurations—afflictive, cognitive, and those of meditative attainment, or alternatively karmic, afflictive, and cognitive—are abandoned separately, respectively on the path of seeing, through the seventh level Far Gone, and at the end of the tenth level.

Here there is one thing to abandon, divided into coarse and subtle, or great, middling, and small. According to whether clear realization is present, what is coarse in a person’s continuum is designated subtle when present in one with realization. Cognitive obscurations too are exclusively the three poisonous afflictions. In the Vast Play, a week after awakening, [the Buddha says]:

Stupidity arising, desire, and anger—
These are like enemies of beings.
I have destroyed them here without remainder.
And the Cloud of Jewels says:

When you abided at awakening’s heart,[^N-B-026]
Desire, hatred, stupidity,
And the many other stains to abandon
Were burned by the fire of your primordial knowing.

notes.problem: Again the source reads byang chung rather than byang chub.
notes.treatment: Render awakening provisionally; retain exact spelling here.
notes.uncertainty: Unverified spelling defect.
notes.review_action: Check witness.

Vajra statement. Others hold that the truth of the nature of phenomena is realized by each higher system refuting the lower, from outsiders through Atiyoga. Taking that as the subject: it follows that the nature of phenomena is not realized, because this is constructed by the conceptual mind and has become an object of comprehension and a valid cognition.[^N-B-027] All tenet systems are views and conceptual mind. That does not know the ultimate. Engaging in Bodhisattva Activity says:

notes.treatment: Preserve the two items without turning the sentence into a doctrinal definition.
notes.uncertainty: An omitted genitive or comparison may be involved.

english: The ultimate is not the conceptual mind’s sphere.
And so forth. The Root Verses on Discerning Knowing say, “Having been embraced by his loving awakened intention …,” and so forth. The Condensed Perfection of Discerning Knowing says:
The Commentary on Valid Cognition says, “When there is a self …,” and so forth. Thus every tenet system obscures seeing ultimate truth.

Vajra statement. Two positions occur: that hearers do not see selflessness, and that they realize it completely. It is also said that because directional parts and moments refute their partless ultimate, they do not see the truth.

Here hearers too see one aspect of the natural state. Without the discerning knowing that realizes the natural state, they could not transcend samsara, just like outsiders. The noble Sutra of the Ten Levels says that they are surpassed by the conceptual mind of the seventh level, Far Gone; this clearly establishes the point. Otherwise they would be surpassed by the conceptual mind of the first level, since [realization] would be absent in hearers and present in bodhisattvas. The master too says:

In the Greater Vehicle, non-arising is taught;
For the others, exhaustion is emptiness.
Since exhaustion and non-arising
Are one in meaning, accept this.
And: “Blessed One, entities and nonentities … knowing …,” and so forth.

Yet their realization is not complete. The paths, results, and qualities of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles are said to differ like the ocean and water in a hoofprint, or space and the space inside a mustard seed eaten by a worm.
Vajra statement. Others say that of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles the Lesser is extremely inferior. The Compendium of the Greater Vehicle says:

Going to hell is not
An enduring obstacle to buddhahood;
The two levels of hearers
And solitary buddhas are enduring obstacles.

On that basis others call it inferior because it does not see the first level’s truth. Here, clear realization through the sixth level is shared with hearers and solitary realizers. The Sutra of the Ten Levels says that the fifth level realizes the four truths, and all scriptures say hearers too realize those. Likewise its statement that the sixth level realizes the twelve links of dependent arising is equal to the statement that solitary buddhas realize them.
For example, the sons of a king and a minister may be the same age. Are their qualities equal? They are not. The Precious Garland says:
In that vehicle of hearers,
“The ordinary mind of awakening …,” and “Without realizing signlessness …,” and so forth.

Vajra statement. Taking as the subject the Ordinary-Mind-Only school’s claim that knowing empty of apprehended object and apprehending subject, self-aware and self-clear, is truly established: others say it is not established as self-aware and self-clear because what is aware and what it is aware of conflict. Object and object-possessor are relative, and self-awareness is not established; therefore they do not see the truth of the nature of phenomena.[^N-B-028]

notes.problem: The school name and rang rig/rang gsal have no complete glossary assignments.
notes.treatment: Use Ordinary-Mind-Only to retain ordinary mind; self-aware and self-clear provisionally preserve awareness and clarity components.
notes.uncertainty: Whether a conventional school name should be an approved whole-expression exception remains open.
notes.review_action: Review these compound proposals; do not activate them globally.

english: Here the Ordinary-Mind-Only school’s clear realization equals the clear realization of the bodhisattva’s seventh level, Far Gone. The Descent to Lanka says:

So it is taught. At the sixth level, discerning knowing becomes manifest: realization of dependent arising in forward and reverse order is called discerning knowing that realizes ignorance. Realizing external and internal phenomena as ordinary mind, one can transform anything; that is the perfection of means.

The Extensive Sutra too says: “Children of the victors, the three realms are ordinary mind alone. The three times too are realized as equal to ordinary mind. That ordinary mind too is comprehended as without edge or center.” This is also explained well in the passage, “The teaching of Ordinary-Mind-Only teaches the Middle Way.”

Vajra statement. Samsara’s root is the personal self, held to be permanent, unitary, and autonomous: strongly clinging to the appropriated aggregates, one apprehends a self as a substance, a succession, an imputation, and so forth. Even without an apprehended personal self, claiming that external and internal phenomena arising merely through dependent arising exist is the self of phenomena. Protector Maitreya and Nagarjuna are said to contradict one another because they maintain, respectively, that its lack of intrinsic nature is realized at the first level and at the eighth.

Here the two do not conflict. Their enlightened intent agrees that the absence of intrinsic nature in the self of phenomena is made manifest at the eighth level. If both kinds of selflessness were realized at the first level, the designation Far Gone would have no application. The enlightened intent concerning the first level is realization that the personal self apprehended in the aggregates lacks intrinsic nature. Realization that even the mere appearance of dependently arising phenomena lacks intrinsic nature—the selflessness of phenomena—occurs at the eighth. Both have the same enlightened intent. The Vast Play says:

When I attained forbearance that here
There is neither birth nor death,
And all these phenomena lack intrinsic nature and self,
Buddha Dipankara gave me his prediction.

And the Sutra of the Questions of Vikurvanaraja says: “Only after realizing the selflessness of phenomena did I see a buddha.” Asked, “Did you not see one during two incalculable eons?” he answered, “I saw the transitory collection.” The Prediction of Dipankara says the same.
Statements that both are realized at the “first” refer to the eighth level, which is first among the pure levels and the youthful levels. Such scriptural passages and reasoning establish this.

Vajra statement. Others maintain that, among the ten levels and five paths, accumulation and preparation are worldly: the name “path” is applied to their cause. Seeing and cultivation are actual paths beyond the world; the final path is the result designated as a path. The ten levels are stages of clear realization. Beginning with the path of seeing, one proceeds through distinct [deep absorptions], such as Heroic Progress and finally the vajralike deep absorption; when the higher is realized, the lower is discarded.
Here one traverses every level and path up to their culmination through the single essence of clear realization of the truth on the path of seeing. The King of Deep Absorption says:

Whoever holds that supreme deep absorption
Will attain Radiant, Hard to Purify, Manifest,
Far Gone, Unmoving, Good Conceptual Mind,
And Cloud of Dharma—the ten levels.

Applied to the four yogas: when co-emergent primordial knowing without elaboration becomes a little clear, there is one-pointedness; seeing its essence is freedom from conceptual elaborations; realizing all appearance as that itself is one taste; realizing equipoise and post-cultivation attainment, or object and object-possessor, as nondual is non-cultivation.[^N-B-029] It is like designating ten stages, differing until one has crossed the eighteen emptinesses and calm abiding.[^N-B-030]

english: Addendum. Some say that although deep absorptions are numerous, vajralike deep absorption is the one at the end of the succession. Here all deep absorptions are vajralike: the path of seeing arises in dependence on the calm-abiding deep absorption of accumulation and preparation, and through it one traverses up to the tenth level.

Vajra statement. Others say: “Immediately upon attaining the first level, one sees a hundred buddhas’ faces and twelve sets of a hundred qualities arise. If you call your one taste pure clear realization, it does not possess even the first level’s qualities.” Here, after attaining a level it must still be purified. There are six alternatives concerning how qualities arise: gradually, all at once, some present and some absent, present but unseen by others, the yogin’s experiential appearances, and scriptural testimony.[^N-B-031]

notes.problem: The initial list is compressed; the following numbered examples clarify six categories.
notes.treatment: Separate six categories using the following examples; experiential appearances renders nyams snang, preserving experience and appearance.
notes.uncertainty: Final two category labels require review.
notes.review_action: Compare list with six explanations.

english: First, qualities arise as described for someone like Shakyamuni, who traversed the path gradually over three incalculable eons.

Second, as with Avalokiteshvara, who is said to have attained the eighth level through a single arousal of the ordinary mind [of awakening]; and the old woman, who attained forbearance concerning non-arising phenomena but had not even the first level’s qualities.[^N-B-032]

notes.problem: The reference is blank; the source repeats mo after old woman.
notes.treatment: Translate from Tibetan, retaining the old-woman example without inventing a personal name.
notes.uncertainty: The repeated syllable and narrative identification are unresolved.
notes.review_action: Check witness and identify the story.

english: Third, some qualities are present and some absent. Although Sudhana’s gurus were on the tenth level, they solemnly declared, “I know nothing beyond this,” and gave their directions.[^N-B-033]

notes.problem: Unusual dbu snyung appears where an oath-taking expression is expected.
notes.treatment: Solemnly declared is a provisional interpretation; directions takes lung bstan in the narrative referral context.
notes.uncertainty: Exact honorific expression and prediction/direction sense uncertain.
notes.review_action: Verify witness and narrative.

english: Fourth, qualities exist but are unseen. Nagarjuna is predicted in the Descent to Lanka as being on the first level, in the Great Drum and Manjushri Root Continuum as being on the eighth, and in the Great Cloud as being on the tenth. Yet no one saw the twelve sets of a hundred qualities and so forth. Similarly, Amitabha abided upon Songtsen’s head and Protector Maitreya on Asanga’s shoulder, but were unseen.
Fifth, as explained in the Ten Levels, what arises in the ordinary mind of awakening is seen only by the person himself, as with Mila.[^N-B-034]

notes.problem: The phrase may mean bodhisattvas’ arising experiences rather than events in bodhicitta; the reference adds no reliable resolution.
notes.treatment: Retain ordinary mind of awakening and mark the attachment as provisional.
notes.uncertainty: Exact subject of what is seen remains uncertain.
notes.review_action: Check witness and the cited explanation.

english: Sixth, sutras and continuums contain testimony that immediately upon attaining a level its qualities arise like the sun and its rays. Therefore one should not cling exclusively to one alternative.
Vajra statement. Others say that the accumulation of primordial knowing, the result, arises from the accumulation of merit, the cause, because Engaging in Bodhisattva Activity states:

All these branches
The Sage taught for the sake of discerning knowing.
And:

As long as that root of virtue is not complete,
That holy awakening will not be exhausted.[^N-B-035]

notes.problem: The source reads will not be exhausted, not will not arise or be attained.
notes.treatment: Keep the supplied verbal meaning, despite the argumentative difficulty.
notes.uncertainty: Possible corrupt quotation.
notes.review_action: Check original quotation and witness.

english: So they argue. Here the two accumulations are united and abide inseparably in all three: The Ground, path, and result. The Play of Manjushri says that even at the time of The Ground, “Ignorance itself is awakening; awakening itself is ignorance.” And the Highest Continuum says:

Because perfect buddha embodiment proliferates,
Because suchness is inseparable,
And because the lineage is present, all embodied beings
Always possess buddha essence.
So it says. On the path too, the Condensed Perfection of Discerning Knowing says:
Discerning knowing goes before giving gifts.

Thus there is primordial knowing in equipoise and the accumulation of merit in post-cultivation attainment. If one holds that they [proceed] one upon the other, it is like setting down the right and left feet while walking on the ground.[^N-B-036]

notes.problem: The relationship between alternation and inseparability is implicit, and goms pa spelling is unusual for steps.
notes.treatment: Use a walking analogy provisionally; bracket proceed.
notes.uncertainty: Whether this is a concession or objection remains uncertain.
notes.review_action: Review exact wording and rhetorical scope.

english: At the result, the two accumulations reach completion and the two embodiments become manifest. The noble master says:
Through this virtue, may all beings …
“Merit …,” and so forth. Otherwise cause and result would belong to different kinds, and it would follow that the ultimate is produced by the relative.

Vajra statement. Others say: “Of the field, intention, and substance of gathering accumulations, those with a less developed continuum should offer to the perfectly pure field, the Three Supreme Ones, since the result is immeasurable. They rely on the field of spiritual friends to make that a cause of renunciation and great liberation. Bodhisattvas with a more developed continuum cherish inferior fields and choose downward.”

Here our position is that, whether the continuum’s development is high or low, one must choose the higher field. A perfectly pure field brings vast temporary and ultimate results; dedication of those roots of virtue to self and others accomplishes great purposes. Giving with the three inferior fields as objects of focus—other [recipients], sentient beings, and those who cause harm—respectively increases afflictions, harms the teaching, and perpetuates harm to oneself.[^N-B-037]

notes.problem: Three lower fields are asserted, but only two clear noun phrases appear; other is treated provisionally as the first.
notes.treatment: Preserve the three outcomes and show supplied recipients in brackets.
notes.uncertainty: Enumeration and causal distribution uncertain.
notes.review_action: Check witness for omitted wording; review threefold list.

english: Then why is it said that a bodhisattva who judges recipients as good or bad does not complete the perfections? Such inferior recipients must be made perfectly pure in the ordinary mind. All phenomena are formations of ordinary mind, like the dependent arising of an image of an embodiment and its object of focus.

Therefore, if one gives to an inferior recipient after arousing the perception of that recipient as a buddha, it will certainly be accomplished accordingly. For people of every degree of development, choosing the higher field and making the inferior field pure is an exceedingly profound essential point.

Vajra statement. Others say that to transcend samsara one must abandon self-apprehension. Here, apprehending as self and thereby gathering accumulations in order to abandon that self-apprehension is maintained to be skillful means.[^N-B-038] By apprehending [things] as one’s own and offering them to the Three Supreme Ones, vast results increase. By giving away what was apprehended as one’s own, one realizes selflessness. By apprehending sentient beings as oneself and giving for their sake, one does not abide in peace. Engaging in Bodhisattva Activity likewise says:

notes.problem: The complete compound has no glossary row; ’dzin pa is apprehending subject, but these clauses use apprehension as an action.
notes.treatment: Use self-apprehension and apprehending as self/one’s own, preserving the apprehending role and the source play on ownership.
notes.uncertainty: The shift between self and ownership is contextually supported but remains a usage proposal.
notes.review_action: Review compound and grammatical usage across this section.

english:
Taking with my conceptual mind all these unowned things,
I offer them well to the Sages, supreme among beings,
Together with their children.
Holy recipients endowed with great compassionate responsiveness,
In loving enlightened intent toward me, accept these things of mine.

So it says. All phenomena of samsara and nirvana are subject to transformation by ordinary mind. Therefore appropriating the happiness, goodness, splendor, and prosperity of samsara and nirvana and gathering accumulations becomes a cause for relinquishing self-apprehension—just as fire arising from wood burns the wood itself. Saraha too says:
Ordinary mind itself alone is the seed of everything.
“Where …,” and so forth, he says.

Vajra statement. Some say one dedicates only virtue one has personally done and gathered, not others’ virtue. Others say that the element of already present virtue cannot be dedicated: whatever merely exists is impermanent; since no phenomenon lies outside the basic space of phenomena, everything would absurdly be virtuous; and since dedication means transformation, if it changed it would become conditioned. Thus, they say, there is nothing to dedicate.

Here, if one gathers the roots of virtue of samsara and nirvana into the single mandala of one’s own ordinary mind and dedicates them, that is what comes about. Suchness is said to be undivided, and arousing the ordinary mind [of awakening] is said to make one master of samsara and nirvana. The roots of virtue from that arousal until the holy Dharma disappears are for sentient beings’ sake; therefore past virtue should be dedicated. The Continuum of the Unmoving One says:

Through the immeasurable, incalculable merit
Gathered by the Blessed One, /[^N-B-039]
May all beings without exception
Attain the unsurpassed state.

notes.problem: A literal slash follows the verse punctuation in the fixed transcript.
notes.treatment: Keep the slash visible as an unresolved source mark.
notes.uncertainty: Its function is unknown.
notes.review_action: Check archival witness; do not delete as tokenizer noise.

english: And the Extensive Mother also teaches dedicating the roots of virtue of the four noble ones.

As for the second position: if mere existence and being accepted entail impermanence, the buddhas’ primordial knowing and ultimate qualities such as their powers would also be impermanent, since they exist and are accepted. If no phenomenon lies outside the basic space of phenomena, why would everything not become stagnant neutrality? The reasoning is the same. Virtue and wrongdoing would then be altogether impossible.[^N-B-040]

notes.problem: Here the term denotes ethical neutrality in an argument, rather than a meditative state.
notes.treatment: Retain canonical stagnant neutrality while flagging its contextual scope.
notes.uncertainty: Whether a scoped ethical-neutrality exception is needed remains open.
notes.review_action: Review this occurrence separately from meditative uses.

english: If dedicating the basic space of phenomena makes everything virtuous and therefore makes it a conditioned object bearing signs, the same applies to virtuous karma; dedication free of poison would become impossible. Dedication must therefore be posited in dependence on the relative: just as merit is made the thing dedicated, it does not proceed according to [ultimately established] characteristics.[^N-B-041] Ultimately, dedication itself is not established, so analysis of whether the basic space of phenomena is something to dedicate does not apply.

notes.problem: The last phrase mtshan ltar mi ’gro is elliptical.
notes.treatment: Supply ultimately established in brackets, provisionally connecting it to the following ultimate/relative contrast.
notes.uncertainty: Possible alternate relation to sign-based apprehension.
notes.review_action: Review construction against source witness.

english: Therefore the basic space of phenomena, suchness, is to be dedicated: one focuses on all virtue as one taste in the basic space of phenomena and aspires to the natural state, the Dharma embodiment. The Dense Array of Adornments says:

The sugata essence, the virtuous element,
Endowed with uncontaminated qualities—
Through dedicating it, the result matures.
And: “That sugata essence is also virtue.” In Vajra Banner’s Dedication: “Gathering all the elements together …,” and:

Dedicate the virtue arising from yoga;
Dedicate your own ordinary mind as well.
And: “Whatever suchness’s intrinsic nature is like, dedicate all actions in that same way.”
The Compendium asks, “What is ultimate virtue?” and answers, “Suchness.” There are limitless scriptural passages, such as “the roots of virtue of our unsurpassed primordial knowing.”

Although the Mother says that all phenomena, from form to omniscience, are unchanging, there is no contradiction: [dedication] relates to purifying the stains of relative delusion. Thus already present virtue is like the ocean, and virtue done and gathered is like its waves. Therefore dedicate both the gathered and the already present virtue of all samsara and nirvana.

Vajra statement. Others say dedication to buddhas and gurus is necessary because faults have been abandoned and qualities perfected.[^N-B-042] Here too dedication for them is certainly necessary, because it speeds the completion of awakened activity, like adding wealth to a wealthy person. The Eight Thousand says:

notes.problem: The objection says necessary, although the reply suggests the opponent may have claimed not necessary.
notes.treatment: Preserve the positive statement without supplying a negative.
notes.uncertainty: Possible missing negative, unverified.
notes.review_action: Check witness and argumentative contrast.

english: Buddhas’ activity does not depend on a single cause or condition; it is like the sound of a vina.[^N-B-043] Nanda and Nandabala offered the concentrated milk of a thousand cows and dedicated it, saying, “May the observance be accomplished”; through this [the Buddha] awakened at dawn. Likewise, when Devadatta’s hurled stone made his foot bleed, Kashyapa’s declaration of truth stopped it.

notes.problem: sgra is canonically word, but denotes an instrument’s audible sound here.
notes.treatment: Sound is an explicitly provisional contextual rendering for this physical simile.
notes.uncertainty: A nonverbal-sound exception is not yet approved.
notes.review_action: Review scoped usage and proposed row, preserving word elsewhere.

english: Gurus too, whether ordinary persons or abiding on the levels, can encounter obstacles; therefore dedication is necessary.
This is the fourth section: the explanation of twenty-five vajra statements and one supplementary shloka, gathering the essential points of the ordinary mind of awakening.

Although others say that secret mantra teachings occur only with this Teacher, time, and realm, here mantra also occurs with other teachers and teachings. To become a buddha oneself one must abandon every coarse and subtle thing to abandon, and teach that to other disciples. Without mantra there would be no antidote for abandoning the subtle. The Manifest Awakening of Vairocana says:[^N-B-044]

notes.problem: Secret mantra, empowerment, samaya, generation/completion stage, and bodhisattva vocabulary lie outside the active glossary’s main Dzogchen-oriented inventory.
notes.treatment: Use these technical expressions provisionally in section 5, with source-linked usage records; retain all covered components such as ordinary mind, discerning knowing, primordial knowing, continuum, and embodiment.
notes.uncertainty: No new technical assignment is owner-approved.
notes.review_action: Review section-5 candidate rows before final terminology approval.

english:
Perfect buddhas who have passed,
Those likewise yet to come,
And protectors now present
Who abide for beings’ benefit—
Knowing this excellent rite,
They attain immeasurable omniscience.
And “the buddhas of the past …,” and so forth. Therefore mantra occurs elsewhere as well.

Addendum. Some say mantra is the fourth scriptural collection, since Excellent Accomplishment says, “Know this from the fourth, the collection of awareness-holders.” Others say it is discipline, because “it disciplines my ordinary mind.” Others say it is sutra, since Subahu says:

I have correctly explained secret mantra
In the manner of sutras; listen with a clear disposition.

So it says. Again, the Continuum of Clear Realization of Dharma Activity teaches outer and inner abhidharma, so some say mantra is inner abhidharma. Although each explains a particular position, most appear to include it chiefly in sutra.

Here mantra is the three scriptural collections, or like the essence of all three. Summarizing what an individual must abandon to awaken, the three trainings—the meaning of the three collections—abandon the three poisons. The union of generation and completion uproots what is to be abandoned, and one awakens in the embodiment of great bliss, the union in which means and discerning knowing are nondual. There is scriptural testimony for all three classifications; on this account they do not conflict, and it is most reasonable.

Vajra statement. Mantra has three: The Ground, the three doors primordially abiding as the three vajras; the path, ripening and liberation; and the result, the four embodiments. The Manjushri Root Continuum says:[^N-B-091]

notes.problem: The glossary display has exceptional capitals The Ground; its status as a prose capitalization rule is unresolved.
notes.treatment: Retain The Ground consistently for technical gzhi in this draft, including section 4; nontechnical ground in walking or geographical compounds is contextual.
notes.uncertainty: Capitalization and broader physical-support senses require editorial review.
notes.review_action: Approve presentation and scoped physical-support uses without changing glossary assignment.

english:
Whoever has not seen the mandala—
The yogin x
With a fist against space x
The water of a mirage x[^N-B-045]

notes.problem: Three literal x marks replace or abbreviate quoted wording.
notes.treatment: Retain x and fragmentary lineation without reconstructing the quotation.
notes.uncertainty: Omitted wording unresolved.
notes.review_action: Compare exact quotation and witness.

english: Thus empowerment must come first. Others say it is attained when the one conferring it is a vajra master of superior, middling, or inferior capacity; the recipient is a person whose continuum has been purified through going for refuge and so forth; and the rite follows the continuums, properly performing the preparatory arrangements and the main rites of the four empowerments: vase, secret, discerning knowing [and primordial knowing], and word.

Here, through the dependent arising of a qualified master teaching instructions to a disciple endowed with confident devotion, the stains of apprehending the three doors as separate are purified. By pointing them out as the three vajras, certainty and realization arise: this is called attaining the empowerment of meaning.

The vase empowerment is the simultaneous arising of certainty that the aggregates, elements, and sense fields are the mandala’s wheel. The secret empowerment is the arising of deep absorption in clarity-emptiness. The empowerment of discerning knowing and primordial knowing concerns bliss-emptiness. The word empowerment is realization of ordinary mind itself as non-arising. When certainty concerning these meanings of empowerment arises in one’s continuum, empowerment is held to have been attained.

Addendum. The three types of person, superior, middling, and inferior, respectively attain empowerment without its being conferred, attain it when it is conferred, and fail to attain it even when it is conferred. Others place the superior faculty first: through confident devotion to the guru, such a person purifies the three doors’ stains and attains empowerment without its being conferred.

Here, although one of superior faculty may have that realization, the rite is certainly necessary because the continuum’s rite is profound. Even with superior faculty the person is unripened, so both master and disciple incur the root downfall of divulging secrets. Like the blind leading the blind, such a person has no authorization to confer empowerment for others. Moreover, the rite is buddhas’ primordial knowing; performing it plants a seed of potency in that person’s continuum.

Empowerment must also be conferred on those of inferior faculty, because a cause in the form of habitual tendencies cannot fail eventually to give its result. There is no way around relying on a vase empowerment, which is like The Ground or a body.

Vajra statement. Others say that, of the four empowerments, the vase empowerment requires an extensive colored-powder mandala with three seats: the seat of buddhas and bodhisattvas, that of awareness women and goddesses, and that of wrathful males and females. If all three are not complete, it cannot be attained through a practice such as Vajrayogini.[^N-B-046]

notes.problem: rig ma is absent as a whole expression; its ritual role is more specific than standalone awareness.
notes.treatment: Awareness woman provisionally preserves the awareness component; no claim that every such figure is a human consort.
notes.uncertainty: Canonical compound and ritual scope pending.
notes.review_action: Review rig ma family and compare section-5 ritual uses.

english: Here buddhas have abandoned the most subtle habitual tendencies and awakened as a single mandala wheel. “Seat” refers to the illusory body as support, with the self-aware ordinary mind of awakening abiding as what is supported.

One’s five aggregates as the five buddhas, and the eight collections [of consciousness] as the eight bodhisattvas, are the seat of buddhas and bodhisattvas. The five elements as the five mothers and eight objects as the eight female bodhisattvas are the seat of awareness women and goddesses. The ten great “words” as the ten wrathful males, and ten objects as the ten wrathful females, are the seat of wrathful males and females.[^N-B-047]

notes.problem: The source reads ten great words, tshig, where bodily joints, tshigs, may be intended; eight collections also omits consciousness explicitly.
notes.treatment: Keep words quoted; disclose consciousness as a bracketed expansion of tshogs brgyad.
notes.uncertainty: Anatomical identification remains unverified.
notes.review_action: Check mandala correspondences against witness; no silent spelling repair.

english: Whether the Yogini has one deity or five, recognizing the aggregates, elements, and sense fields as buddhas means attaining the vase empowerment; in dependence on that, the other three empowerments are attained. The hundred families, five families, three families, and so forth are included in one family.

If one objects, “Though complete implicitly, they are not explicitly complete, so empowerment is not attained,” then except through Manjuvajra it could not be attained through Kalachakra, Guhyasamaja, Chakrasamvara, or Hevajra either, because those are not explicitly complete.[^N-B-048] Therefore, whether the deity number completes one grouping or comprises a single family, empowerment can be conferred and attained.

notes.problem: Four abbreviated title stems appear, and phyogs ’dog in the conclusion is uncertain.
notes.treatment: Expand the title stems as Kalachakra, Guhyasamaja, Chakrasamvara, Hevajra; grouping provisionally renders phyogs ’dog.
notes.uncertainty: Title expansions are contextually strong; final phrase uncertain.
notes.review_action: Confirm titles and the grouping phrase in the witness.

english: Addendum. Although others maintain that the three embodiments are determined as three kinds of deeds and are inconceivable, here a single deity too accomplishes all awakened activities. Their essence is one and their activities are included without interruption. The Two Examinations says:

From the single great ordinary mind
The five aspects of form are displayed;
From those very five families
Many thousands arise.
Therefore all these have one intrinsic nature.
So it says. Even the single family of awakened mind contains all five: embodiment, speech, awakened mind, qualities, and activity.[^N-B-049]

notes.problem: Standalone thugs lacks an established mapping.
notes.treatment: Awakened mind remains a provisional honorific rendering in section 5, distinct from sems ordinary mind and dgongs pa enlightened intent.
notes.uncertainty: Not authorized as a universal equivalent.
notes.review_action: Review thugs in the embodiment/speech/mind grouping and linked occurrences.

english:
The defining character of every mantra
Abides in the sugatas’ awakened mind.
So it says. Since one deity encompasses all families, it can accomplish all four awakened activities.

Addendum. Although others hold that each deity has one definite name, here all deities’ names are assigned in terms of the result made manifest or awakened activity. Therefore even one’s single special deity, such as Chakrasamvara, bears all those names. They are one in purifying obscurations through the path and awakening as the essence of the result’s qualities; in possessing an embodiment with marks and signs and awakened mind with the primordial knowing that is the result of separation [from obscurations]; in being called “Blessed One”; and in caring for those who supplicate them.

Vajra statement. The third empowerment, that of discerning knowing and primordial knowing, is said to be received through the seal of another’s body. In the main rite the master’s instructions and subsequent teaching point out the deep absorption of the four joys, bliss-emptiness. Maitripa regards the certainty arising in this way as example primordial knowing, Naropa as meaning primordial knowing; Marpa says this depends on whether that very [reality] is realized. Some accept it as example, others as meaning primordial knowing.[^N-B-050]

notes.problem: The empowerment name and example/meaning primordial-knowing pair lack complete entries.
notes.treatment: Preserve discerning knowing, primordial knowing, and meaning components in the provisional compound names; seal of another’s body renders the physical ritual expression without adding instructions.
notes.uncertainty: Complete technical names require approval.
notes.review_action: Review compound rows and their relationship to canonical components.

english: Here, unless primordial knowing that realizes the meaning of empowerment beyond the conceptual mind has arisen in one’s continuum, the example does not make that meaning comprehensible. All experiential acquaintance that indicates a similarity through something similar is constructed by the conceptual mind. Accomplishment of Primordial Knowing says:

The bliss of joining the two organs
Ordinary people call that very [reality];
But the victors have not said
That it is great bliss.
So it says. Phagmo Drupa says:

Contaminated bliss, at the great gateway …
A limb of great bliss …[^N-B-051]

notes.problem: The abbreviated quotation has an unclear che sgo construction.
notes.treatment: Keep the fragment and a provisional literal great gateway rather than invent omitted verse.
notes.uncertainty: Word division and intended predicate uncertain.
notes.review_action: Identify full Phagmo Drupa quotation.

english: And so forth. Therefore one cannot categorically determine it as either example or meaning. If feeling is realized as co-emergent primordial knowing beyond the conceptual mind, it is example or meaning; if not realized, it is neither.

Addendum. Concerning the third empowerment there are four claims: primordial knowing in one’s continuum is not realized through bliss of a similar kind; since it is realized without error it is no different from buddhas’ primordial knowing; it is meaning primordial knowing when bliss-emptiness of equal taste is experienced inexpressibly; or only one ray of the path of seeing’s primordial knowing arises. Those hoping for a better understanding say it realizes a mere reflection. Yangdak Lha says:

Whatever arises in the third moment
Is not seeing meaning; with the result-bearing [factor]
It is sullied, like molasses.[^N-B-052]

notes.problem: The molasses simile and ’bras can, result-bearing, are unclear in the fragment.
notes.treatment: Translate literally and disclose factor as grammatical supply.
notes.uncertainty: Possible defective reading or incomplete analogy.
notes.review_action: Locate complete quotation and verify witness.

english: Thus each accepts one or the other, example or meaning. Because it is contaminated bliss, they say one must engage without being stained by the fifth root downfall. Here, at those four times or occasions, there is no occasion permitting [breach of] root samaya. The reason is as the Great Brahmin says:

Until yesterday I was not a monk;
From today onward I am a monk.

Accordingly, if realization of co-emergent primordial knowing, the equal taste of happiness and suffering, arises in one’s continuum, there is no need to say that it is example and meaning primordial knowing. But under the influence of degeneration, most people invoke the path and earlier masters’ deeds as a pretext while engaging solely in the afflicted tactile pleasure of contaminated sexual union. Those hoping for something better may have bliss arise as co-emergent; yet unless all feeling arises as co-emergent, suffering [must also] arise as co-emergent. If it does not, all the gathered “realizations” are not realized as the nature of phenomena; the third empowerment’s purpose is empty, and root downfalls of sutra and mantra are accomplished.[^N-B-053] Hevajra likewise says:

notes.problem: The conditional around suffering is compressed, and rtogs tshogs reads gathered realizations where a conceptual-thought collection might be expected.
notes.treatment: Retain realizations in quotation marks; mark must also as a contextual supply.
notes.uncertainty: No spelling emendation accepted.
notes.review_action: Check the conditional and rtogs/tog reading against witness.

english:
Without semen there is no bliss;
Without bliss, that is absent.
And Lord Jowo says:

Because the Great Primordial Buddha [Continuum]
Emphatically prohibits them,
The secret empowerment and empowerment of discerning knowing
Must not be received by those practising celibacy.
Further, in our own system the three vows have one essential point, and what is prohibited is prohibited from the outset. Therefore they should not be received from the beginning.

Vajra statement. Of generation and completion, the liberating path for the ripened, the first is discussed in terms of three characteristics. The nature of phenomena is the thoroughly established; dependence on assembled conditions is the other-powered; and imputing what is not so as so is the imputed. In cultivation of a meaning generalization’s aspect, of the two, succession and imputation, it is the former.[^N-B-054] The cultivating knowing is other-powered; since [the deity] is absent in actuality, contriving what is not so as so is imputation. Others compare it to Nagabodhi cultivating a tree and its appearing.

notes.problem: The three-characteristics list lacks separators; the succession/imputation contrast is particularly unclear.
notes.treatment: Segment the standard three listed characteristics provisionally; retain the later contrast literally and bracket deity as contextual subject.
notes.uncertainty: The referent of former and the interpretation of rgyun remain unresolved.
notes.review_action: Check original punctuation and any omitted words; review three characteristic terms as proposed glossary rows.

english: Here generation-stage deities are thoroughly established from the beginning, because diligent practice accomplishes them—just as smelting gold ore produces gold. Otherwise they could not be accomplished, just as smelting ordinary stone does not produce gold.

If something could be accomplished by imputing what is not so as so, outsiders too would realize the natural state, since they presume what is not the natural state to be it. Therefore all aggregates, elements, and sense fields have primordially abided as the mandala wheel. Hevajra says:

Through the power of these, sentient beings
Are undoubtedly buddhas.
The ten months extend the levels;
Sentient beings are lords of the ten levels.[^N-B-055]

notes.problem: The phrase says ten months extend levels; its ritual/embryological relation is not explicit.
notes.treatment: Keep months and levels without replacing either by a more familiar formula.
notes.uncertainty: Verb and comparison remain uncertain.
notes.review_action: Verify the Hevajra quotation.

english: Guhyasamaja says:

In brief, the five aggregates
Are renowned as the five buddhas.
And Universal Activity says, “These beings are the identity of the five buddhas.” The Ocean of Secrets says:

All these mandalas of the knowable, without exception,
Are the thoroughly established three embodiments: the secret-mantra vehicle.
Entering the three embodiments’ realm is the vehicle of the path.
The three embodiments without meeting or parting are the vajra vehicle.
So it says.

Addendum. Others say one cannot enter deity [practice] at the outset, but must cultivate through training in purification, alternation, illusion, and so forth. First one purifies through regarding the environment as the immeasurable palace and its inhabitants as male and female deities. In the middle one trains in alternating those two, and finally in mere illusion. Only then, they say, does cultivation of one’s own body as deity become clear.

Here, because generation stage is thoroughly established, entering all at once into the inseparability of one’s own body and the deity is the profound essential point. The awareness-holder’s vow is not to let body, speech, and mental faculty slip into ordinary [appearance] for even an instant.
Addendum. Concerning accomplishing the deity, Samputa says:

Recite a hundred thousand for the lord of the wheel,
And likewise ten thousand for those of the mandala.

On that basis, others say approach recitation is foremost. Here, too, one must know with certainty that accomplishment comes from the full assembly of dependent-arising factors, with the thoroughly established generation stage as The Ground.

The inner dependent-arising factors are the five manifest awakenings: emptiness as The Ground, the moon as seat, syllables as speech, the emblem as awakened mind, and the fully complete embodiment. The five aggregates’ inherent presence is the cause; the guru’s pointing out through vase empowerment is the condition. Knowing that it is thoroughly established through the power of this assembly constitutes outer and inner dependent arising.
The number of approach recitations is only one part of this.

Addendum. Others say: “Without hardship one does not awaken; austerity must be like ‘water-drinking stone.’[^N-B-056] Relying on sense pleasures makes the body arrogant and generates afflictions; when the body declines, they do not arise. When afflictions arise, one should abase and censure oneself.”

notes.problem: Water-drinking stone is obscure and may conceal a name or damaged expression.
notes.treatment: Retain the literal phrase in quotation marks.
notes.uncertainty: Identification unresolved.
notes.review_action: Check witness and any ascetic example intended.

english: Here such ascetic activity amounts to disparagement, because it imputes an ordinary body. Generation stage is thoroughly established; Buddhists chiefly discipline the ordinary mind within; and [such disparagement] incurs a root downfall. “Completely discipline your own ordinary mind,” it is said. Shantideva says:

Apart from the observance of guarding ordinary mind,
What use are many observances?
And: “The aggregates are the identity of the five buddhas.” Therefore, when ordinary mind is disciplined, body and speech too become disciplined.

Vajra statement. Some say that those with the power of former training, whose previous karmic impetus has awakened, can develop deep absorption without relying on a spiritual friend or instructions, so entry rites are unnecessary. Here even those in whom deep absorption arises naturally in this way need the entry rites exactly as explained, from going for refuge to empowerment. Superimpositions about whether [their experience] is genuine are cut through, and further development expands it still more, like adding wood to a blazing fire.[^N-B-092]

notes.problem: The compound las ’phro has no complete row; standalone ’phro is proliferation.
notes.treatment: Karmic impetus is a provisional whole-compound rendering for residual force of former practice.
notes.uncertainty: A whole-expression exception is proposed, not active glossary terminology.
notes.review_action: Review compound and relation to proliferation family.

english: Thus going for refuge impresses the Buddhist seal; individual liberation gives definite emergence from samsara; arousing the ordinary mind [of awakening] prevents deviation into the hearer or solitary-realizer path; and mantra empowerment reverses the three doors’ collapse into an ordinary state. Pointing out the meaning of great bliss, inseparable from the deep absorption of generation and completion, brings attainment of supreme and common accomplishments.

Although a human body is attained through previously guarding ethical discipline, without continuing the proliferation of virtue and practising on that support, one falls into lower destinies. It is like that.

Vajra statement. Others say mantra deities conform to disciples: paired in union for those with desire, wrathful for those with hatred, and bearing animal heads for those with stupidity, and so appear even without major and minor marks.

Here all deities possess the qualities of major and minor marks through their intrinsic nature, and they must be cultivated that way.[^N-B-057] They are buddhas who have abandoned faults and completed qualities. Cultivating them with excellent marks completes the accumulations; without those marks, faults arise. Kalachakra says:

notes.problem: The instrumental construction requires a grammatical relationship; the glossary protects intrinsic nature but has no universally approved adverbial formula.
notes.treatment: Through their intrinsic nature is a local provisional construction, retaining the full lexical commitment.
notes.uncertainty: Its exact causal versus inherent force requires review.
notes.review_action: Approve or revise this construction locally without dropping intrinsic nature.

english:
The supreme lord of victors’
Thirty-two major marks
And eighty excellent minor signs—
All gathered without exception—
Constitute the supreme sovereign’s state,
Which mantra practitioners should cultivate.
The Vajra Pavilion says, “That embodiment adorned with thirty-two excellent marks and eighty minor signs is me.” Hevajra says:

In the queen’s bhaga, the abode of bliss,
The Teacher with thirty-two marks,
The chief with eighty minor signs,
Abides in the aspect called “Guwa.”[^N-B-058]

notes.problem: Guwa is not securely identified in the supplied quotation.
notes.treatment: Retain Guwa in transliteration, without reconstructing a Sanskrit word.
notes.uncertainty: Reading and referent unresolved.

english: Such passages are limitless. Without understanding this manner, cultivating paired deities in union, terrifying deities, or animal aspects while motivated by the three poisons is no different from propitiating gyal and sen spirits. Even if stability is attained, not a single quality arises.

Vajra statement. Others say that whether cultivating a deity oneself, showing it to others, or painting its embodiment, one should reproduce whatever face one has seen through strenuous practice. Here one must chiefly follow only those deities’ forms, proportions, and other features exactly as taught in stainless sutras and continuums, since the knower of all knowable things teaches all sentient beings the means of abandoning faults and accomplishing qualities.

What is wrong with the deity one has oneself seen? One’s continuum is obscured; the fourfold combination of afflictions produces various visual appearances. Unless what one sees is brought into accordance with the victors’ word, one does not know whether it leads to good or harm; it is mistaken knowing that conflicts with their word.[^N-B-059]

notes.problem: The fourfold combination of afflictions is not explained here.
notes.treatment: Preserve four without importing a classification.
notes.uncertainty: Exact grouping unresolved.
notes.review_action: Check source and doctrinal referent.

english: Vajra statement. Others assign respectively to superior, middling, and inferior faculties: mandalas of heaps, painted cloth, and colored powder; generation stage completed through instantaneous recollection, through a seed syllable, and through cultivating the elements in successive layers; and no rite, a middling rite, and an extensive rite. For superior faculties, they say, the first in each of the three groups—heaps and so forth—is sufficient.

Here an extensive rite is especially necessary for those of superior faculty. Realization of non-arising depends on the dependent arising of cause and result; when it is realized, it appears as cause and result, and all qualities and awakened activities arise. Those of inferior faculty do not know how to engage in this way. The Mother says:
“Because all phenomena are evenness, the perfection of discerning knowing is evenness.” Also: “Because space is boundless x”; “Mount Meru’s diversity x.”[^N-B-060]

notes.problem: Two quoted fragments end in literal x marks.
notes.treatment: Retain x and do not invent completion.
notes.uncertainty: Missing wording unresolved.
notes.review_action: Identify full quotations and compare witness.

english: These statements teach that point.

Addendum. Other scholars say: “Doing, Activity, and Yoga are not profound, while Unsurpassed is profound, because the former have interpretable meaning and the latter definitive meaning.”[^N-B-061] Here we agree that it is definitive meaning; nevertheless both the three of interpretable meaning and Unsurpassed of definitive meaning require extensive rites. Without causes and conditions there is no accomplishment, just as a seed without water, manure, warmth, and moisture does not grow.

notes.problem: The continuum-class names are abbreviated and lack established whole-expression rows.
notes.treatment: Use Doing, Activity, Yoga, and Unsurpassed provisionally, preserving the glossary doing/activity components rather than substituting class names without traceability.
notes.uncertainty: Reader-facing titles and interpretive/definitive distinction require review.
notes.review_action: Review whole-expression candidates and compare occurrences.

english: Therefore the definitive meaning—that one’s own body is primordially the three vajras—must be realized through rites. Once realized, the methods of interpretable meaning, such as rites, become one taste with definitive meaning.

Addendum. Others say one must enter through an extensive rite at the very outset of empowerment. Here a concise rite too is accepted if that concise method can discipline clinging to signs. When ordinary mind is held on a single realization and the guru points it out, realization is attained without difficulty, as with Nagabodhi and others.[^N-B-062]

notes.problem: rtogs pa, realization, is supplied where a single conceptual focus might seem more natural.
notes.treatment: Retain realization and do not conflate it with rtog pa conceptual thought.
notes.uncertainty: Possible spelling or syntactic issue unresolved.
notes.review_action: Check witness and compare Nagabodhi narrative.

english: This comes from the assembled dependent-arising factors: a qualified guru, the disciple’s confident devotion, and previous training.

Addendum. Of the two hindrances to mantra, enemies and obstructors, others consider it profound to cultivate protection against obstructors as a wheel containing a mountain of fire, a vajra fence, ten wrathful deities, and an immeasurable palace. Here those are partial. The extraordinary protection wheel is the nondual ordinary mind of awakening. In ultimate truth, it is said, there are neither obstructors nor even a buddha.

Although they do not exist, obstructing appearances arise from the assembly of object, faculty, and knowing. Their root is the mental faculty’s sense field: the eye and other faculties are taken together with mental consciousness, giving the six that arise and spread toward external form. Eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental faculty are taught as six vajras encompassing all sense fields of stupidity, hatred, miserliness, desire, and jealousy, respectively.[^N-B-063]

notes.problem: Six faculties are paired with five named afflictions; the combination with mental consciousness is compressed.
notes.treatment: Keep all six and all five without inventing a sixth affliction; preserve the source respectively.
notes.uncertainty: Distribution and sense-field construction need review.
notes.review_action: Check the six-vajra mapping against witness.

english: Outwardly, the eye is Kshitigarbha and its family Vairocana. Through habituation and familiarity with this as one’s own Kshitigarbha, all that is seen does not depart from Vairocana; what is called an obstruction has never been established.

Likewise apply the remaining five as above: the ear and so on are respectively Lord of Secrets, Akashagarbha, Avalokiteshvara, Dispeller of Obscurations, and Samantabhadra, who gathers the sense fields. Their families are Akshobhya, Ratnasambhava, Amitabha, Amoghasiddhi, and, as the sixth, Vajradhara.

Inwardly, the five primordial knowings—mirrorlike, basic space of phenomena, evenness, discriminating primordial knowing, and accomplishing activity—subdue the five ignorances to be abandoned: stupidity, hatred, miserliness, desire, and jealousy. They do so without removing or installing anything, without setting up an object to abandon and an antidote; this suffices as protection. “Protection” means protecting through the path what abides as cause, and thereby making the result manifest.[^N-B-064]

notes.problem: Only the discriminating primordial-knowing compound is established as a whole expression; the other four are abbreviated.
notes.treatment: Use full primordial knowing across the five and preserve basic space of phenomena/evenness/activity components; sor rtog is identified as the established discriminating expression.
notes.uncertainty: Full names and lexical-family realization pending.
notes.review_action: Review proposed compound records and the source mapping order.

english: Vajra statement. Others say the extensive presentations of the preliminary and main ripening rites, liberating generation and completion stages, and so on are taught for those who enjoy elaboration. Here all those stages of elaboration are naturally occurring dependent-arising factors present in the character of the knowable. The five in the outer environment—wind, fire, water, earth, and Mount Meru—are taught as the soles, genitals, navel, chest, and spinal joints of one’s own body; one must cultivate them accordingly.

As for the formation of the inhabitants, cultivating male and female deities’ intrinsic nature as primordially established makes the result, evenness, manifest. These elaborations abide primordially and arise through dependent arising. Likewise:

Other than dependent arising,
There is no phenomenon whatsoever.
And the Kila Continuum Rays of the Sun says:

Through phenomena abiding as dependent arising,
Awareness’s primordial knowing becomes clear.
So it says.

Vajra statement. Others say the vajra body’s natural state consists of channels that form and abide together with the body, moving winds, and the arrangement of the ordinary mind of awakening’s spheres in four wheels.[^N-B-065] Here the profound vajra body is held to be the nondual wheel, because it is the Dharma embodiment, like a diamond endowed with seven assertions. The Vajra Peak says:

notes.treatment: Preserve the protected ordinary mind component and sphere, while flagging the physical contextual use explicitly.

english:
Hard, substantial, without a hollow interior,
Not to be broken or destroyed,
Not to be burned, without fear—
Emptiness is explained as vajra.

Thus it is the Dharma embodiment together with qualities and deeds. One who never lets the three doors depart from the three vajras is called a vajra-holder. Through this, making manifest the inseparable three doors as the indivisible vajra of nonduality is called the vajra body.

The bodyless body, the supreme body;
The one who realizes the body’s limit.
As this states, it is the manifestation of that.

Vajra statement. Others say the natural state of channels, winds, and spheres is determined solely by what the continuums teach. Here Vajradhara concealed certain profound aspects of the natural state by scrambling the continuums, twisting the scriptural transmissions, and hiding the instructions.[^N-B-066] Sharp-facultied people who enter through intellectual understanding without relying on a guru will fail to attain accomplishment and will deteriorate.

notes.treatment: Preserve the three parallel actions provisionally.
notes.uncertainty: Exact second verb uncertain.
