english: Dharma depends on scriptural transmission; transmission on instructions; instructions on lineage gurus. The meaning is concealed so that those of sharp faculties realize its profundity by relying on a guru and practising diligently. The Vajra Essence says:

The eighty thousand Dharma collections
And four thousand, counted in thousands,[^N-B-067]
I have taught as perfectly gathered.
This meaning is not proclaimed elsewhere;
So that disciples who respect
Their gurus may realize it,
It is concealed in other continuums.

notes.problem: The source repeats thousand in an unusual counting clause.
notes.treatment: Retain the repeated quantity rather than normalize to a conventional 84,000 formula.
notes.uncertainty: Likely defective quotation.
notes.review_action: Verify exact verse.

english: The manner of realization is like that of the precious Dharma Lord.

Vajra statement. Others say that because the body’s faults and qualities arise from the dependent arising of channels and winds, the continuum teachings on the causes of its initial formation, The Ground of its intervening abiding, and the conditions of its final destruction are profound.

Here the medical continuums are held to be profound concerning certain modes of presence and functioning of channels and winds—the doing, doer, and activity. They explain clearly what the mantra continuums conceal and do not teach clearly. For example, the Eight Branches explains initial formation according to whichever of the three poisons predominates, the three disorders’ “skin,” their alterations, the respective antidotes and means of clearing them that purify faults and generate benefit and happiness, and which wind abides in which channel.[^N-B-068]

notes.problem: The source literally reads the three disorders’ skin; a formation verb might have been intended.
notes.treatment: Retain skin in quotation marks; do not silently repair.
notes.uncertainty: Medical clause uncertain.
notes.review_action: Check the medical citation and Tibetan witness.

english: This too is buddhas’ awakened activity: the meaning taught in scriptures such as Golden Light and explained by the bodhisattvas of the three families, master Nagarjuna, and others.

Vajra statement. Others regard going for refuge, the Dharma wheel of the four truths, the discipline collection, the training in ethical discipline, the individual-liberation vow, arousing the ordinary mind [of awakening], the ultimate, Unsurpassed Continuum, the fourth empowerment, the liberating path, and completion stage as profound, and other things as not profound.[^N-B-069]

notes.problem: The list includes practices that the following response calls underestimated; its internal division is unclear.
notes.treatment: Retain all named items and the explicit profound/not-profound contrast without silently inserting negatives into the list.
notes.uncertainty: Possibly missing connectors or a contrast boundary.
notes.review_action: Review list punctuation and argument against witness.

english: Here those practices others regard as not profound are made profound. Without them one cannot attain even the path’s qualities, let alone buddhahood, like branches and leaves severed from the root. Therefore going for refuge is profound, because it is the foundational Ground of all Dharma—just as a universal monarch must first be born into the proper family in order to appear in the world.
Thereafter the four truths, discipline, and so forth are profound, just as that [monarch] must rely on special wheels of Dharma, crafts, letters, and reckoning. Lord Jigten Gonpo says:

Though others call higher rites and empowerments profound,
My child, I place great weight on the vase empowerment.[^N-B-070]
It is like The Ground, a vessel, and a body;
The others are its special qualities.

notes.problem: Reference is blank; ’am bu and rtsi chod are unusual.
notes.treatment: Translate directly with provisional vocative my child and place great weight.
notes.uncertainty: Exact dialectal expression uncertain.
notes.review_action: Check Jigten Gonpo quotation and witness.

english: So he says. The Two Examinations likewise teaches from “First, confer restoration and purification,” through to “After that, commence Hevajra.”

Vajra statement. Others say the practices just described as not profound are unnecessary: practising channels and winds progressively dissolves the four courses, traverses up to the tenth level, makes manifest the result’s four embodiments and five primordial knowings, and attains Vajradhara’s state.

Here, without those supposedly unprofound practices, instructions on channels and winds do not bring buddhahood, because the supporting Ground is absent. A universal monarch likewise cannot live without food. A diligent person might attain some higher knowing and miraculous powers, but outsiders have these too; even they require freedom from desire, which appears difficult nowadays.

Addendum. Although others regard mantra’s distinctive instructions on channels and winds as profound, here discipline surpasses the essential point of any mantra instruction. Restraining the three doors’ faults makes body, speech, and mental faculty workable. It purifies the faults: unchastity in body and channels, falsehood in speech and winds, covetous ordinary mind and the rest in mental faculty and spheres. The pure essence of qualities increases, filling the four wheels; the four meditative stabilities, four results of spiritual discipline, and ultimately the powers and other qualities arise.

If the three doors are not purified, the three poisons make them turbid. A monk’s firm ordinary mind of restraint restrains all three—channels, winds, and spheres. This is also why the four wheels are related to the four schools.[^N-B-071]

notes.problem: The four schools are not identified in this passage.
notes.treatment: Retain the number and generic school designation without naming traditions.
notes.uncertainty: Exact schools and relation unresolved.

The all-basis, the sugata essence, is realized only partially even at the tenth level, like an elephant in a dark enclosure. “Like the sun in a sky where clouds are seen …”; “Here even you intelligent noble ones, whose conceptual mind’s eye is pure, do not see all.”[^N-B-072] This accords with the general position.

english: Here, however, through diligently cultivating the meaning of instructions taught by a guru endowed with blessing, the all-basis is sometimes seen in another way. When familiarization reaches the essential point, the elements gather inward. One sees in the body the seeds of habitual tendencies as channel knots, and the seeds of the six awarenesses abiding as syllables. When winds enter there, the six families are seen at their respective places. Through long familiarization, one sees the six awarenesses’ mandalas outwardly and much of what arises from particular outer causes and conditions. This is seeing the all-basis, or the nature of phenomena, the sugata essence, because phenomena’s dependent arising is made manifest.[^N-B-073]

notes.treatment: Preserve awarenesses where rig is supplied and families where rigs is supplied.

english: Purifying the all-basis, afflicted mental faculty, mental consciousness, and five gates gives rise to the five primordial knowings: basic space of phenomena, mirrorlike, evenness, and the rest. Therefore one must distinguish the senses of all-basis that is not seen even at the tenth level, seen at the seventh, seen at the first, and seen by ordinary persons.

Vajra statement. Others call profound a great cultivator’s experiential acquaintance even when it occurs in a form explained in neither the Buddha’s word nor treatises. Here experiential acquaintance conflicting with the word is mistaken conceptual thought, since it conflicts with the omniscient one’s speech or has taken up an outsider’s path. It is like outsiders’ tenets imputed through higher knowing, concerning the destruction of the former limit and nondestruction of the latter.[^N-B-074]

english: An experience opposed to the speech of the Buddha, who has great knowing and love, is the work of “bowing” [apparently Mara].[^N-B-075] Understand this according to the Mother and the Nine-Volume Ushnisha.

english: Vajra statement. Others say that because the scriptural collections and continuum classes, and interpretable and definitive meanings, differ, what is prohibited in one is permitted in another, and what is abandoned in one is accomplished in another. Partial agreement is sufficient, and lower teachings are discarded on entering higher ones.

Here one must understand all enlightened intent as free of contradiction. The eighty thousand Dharma collections were taught as antidotes to afflictions; all must be practised to abandon faults and accomplish qualities. The three vows and Mahamudra have the same essential point of ethical discipline, and the meaning they express is one. The Moon Lamp says:

Whatever sutras I have taught,
Their syllables differ, but their meaning is one.
And Jowo says:

The eighty thousand Dharma collections
And the four thousand that were taught
All incline and flow into this nature of phenomena.
Therefore they must be understood without contradiction.

Vajra statement. Others say the faults and qualities of practice concern particular instructions and occur solely according to them. Here they are held to occur according to the omniscient victor’s word, rather than merely according to instructions. Through direct perception of every dependent arising of cause and result, he knows precisely which essential points generate qualities and abandon faults, and teaches them to disciples with great love. Thus they occur exactly as scripture states.

Vajra statement. Others accept three deep absorptions as causes of the three embodiments: non-conceptuality, in which not even the slightest conceptual thought moves; bliss, in which even a knife-strike to the body is blissful; and clarity, without distinction of outer, inner, or individual.

Here those three faultless deep absorptions are causes or seeds of samsara’s three realms: bliss gives birth in the desire realm, clarity in the form realm, and non-conceptuality in the formless realm. Aryadeva says:

Although the forest fire of meditative stability repeatedly burns afflictions’ thicket,
Because the firm root of self-view is not abandoned,
It grows again at once, as if watered by rain.
Protector Phagmo Drupa too says:

In the ocean of bliss and clarity
Abides the jewel of clinging and the apprehending subject.
If strong clinging to that jewel arises,
Hell’s guardians, like poisonous snakes,
Cut off the life of great bliss
And cast one into a terrifying abyss.

Accordingly, I think what is needed is the three as inseparable, of equal taste in the basic space of phenomena. Though elsewhere they are described as faultless, I wonder whether the enlightened intent is that they have not gone beyond conceptual thought apprehending bliss, clarity, and the rest separately.[^N-B-090]

notes.problem: sems functions here as the finite verb think, not a noun denoting ordinary mind.
notes.treatment: Render I think as a local grammatical/contextual use, preserving the author’s tentative stance.
notes.uncertainty: No blanket exception to ordinary mind is implied.
notes.review_action: Review the finite verbal use separately from noun occurrences.

english: Vajra statement. Using a mandala wheel such as Chakrasamvara as illustration, others say [the principal deity] is the complete enjoyment embodiment, the mother is the Dharma embodiment, and the heroes, dakinis, and gate and intermediate-direction goddesses of the awakened-mind, speech, and embodiment wheels abiding at the twenty-four places are the emanation embodiment; these three are distinct.[^N-B-076]

notes.problem: The first embodiment’s subject is omitted; the following mother/Dharma-embodiment relation is compressed.
notes.treatment: Supply principal deity visibly, with the subsequent correspondences parsed in source order. Abbreviated embodiment names use established complete expressions.
notes.uncertainty: First subject and attachment require review.

english: Here each of the three embodiments includes the other two. The mandala, together with its eight charnel grounds, abides in one’s own body. Through cultivating it as the path, the aggregates, elements, and sense fields become perfectly pure, and there is no separation within that wheel. The Ocean of Secrets says:

The thoroughly established three embodiments are the secret-mantra vehicle.
Entering those three embodiments is the vehicle of the path.
The three embodiments without meeting or parting are the resultant vehicle.
So it teaches.
Vajra statement. Others say: “Since the Sage’s and Vajradhara’s teachings, sutra and mantra, are distinct, mantra does not require ethical discipline. Guhyasamaja says:

Relying on the five kinds
Of sense pleasure, accomplishment comes swiftly.
And, “You should kill living beings,” and so forth.”[^N-B-077]

One endowed with the five training rules,
The bodhisattva vow,
And secret-mantra samaya
Is a lay vajra-holder.

The ten trainings x
The bodhisattva’s x
Secret mantra x
A novice x[^N-B-078]

Ten million trainings x
Awakening x

A fully ordained monk x[^N-B-079]

english: Also, from “First, confer restoration and purification,” through “After that, commence Hevajra.” And the Manjushri Root Continuum says:
With corrupted ethical discipline, mantra is not accomplished.
So it says.

Vajra statement. Others say that in mantra entry, path, and result are blissful, so accomplishment comes through enjoying sense pleasures. Here sutra and mantra are the same regarding desire’s obstructing power. In the vehicle of characteristics, the Mother says: “If desire obstructs even birth in Brahma’s world, what need to mention nirvana?” Also: “Desires are like poisonous leaves, a sword’s edge, and a cavity of filth.” And, as just explained, ethical discipline is indispensable in mantra.
The Higher Examination says: “Blessed One, what is impure?” He replied, “The five, form and the rest.” Asked why, he said, “Because their essence is apprehension of form.”
The Heap of Jewels says:

Whatever obstructing qualities
I have taught to people,
All those I declare truly:
They do not become otherwise.

So it says. Instructions to rely on sense pleasures concern a person with a powerful antidote, whose continuum is not stained, like a lotus in mud. Yet this appears far more difficult than the vehicle of characteristics. Therefore this swordlike mantra deteriorates if it does not rely on shieldlike ethical discipline.

Vajra statement. Others say that discipline abandons The Ground, the vehicle of characteristics purifies The Ground, and mantra transforms The Ground: desire is transformed into the path as blissful deep absorption, whose result is complete enjoyment embodiment; hatred and stupidity are transformed into the path as deep absorptions of clarity and non-conceptuality, whose results are emanation embodiment and Dharma embodiment. Thus, they say, differentiating conceptualization is the play of primordial knowing.

Here, if it is claimed that mantra’s path transforms nonvirtue into virtue, there is no occasion for such transformation. Although the mandala wheel is primordial, adventitious stains obscure it, and the path removes or purifies those stains. Hevajra says:

Sentient beings are buddhas,
Yet obscured by adventitious stains.
When those are removed, they are buddhas.

Thus it is a path of purification. Moreover, in the vehicle of characteristics too, the Extensive Sutra’s silk scroll containing the three-thousandfold world and the Essence Sutra’s nine examples teach this and the like. [The supplied text then says:] it is not a path of abandonment; it is a path of transformation.[^N-B-080]

notes.problem: The affirmative transformation conflicts with the adjacent rejection of transformation and conclusion purification.
notes.treatment: Retain the affirmative statement and make the inconsistency visible; silk scroll/world is a provisional interpretation of stong gsum dar yug.
notes.uncertainty: Possible lost negative or changed term, unverified.
notes.review_action: Check witness and both scriptural similes; do not harmonize silently.

english: If, unlike that, it were a path of transformation, it would conflict with “He is called Blessed One because he has conquered the Maras, thorough affliction and the rest.” The three poisons are not established as The Ground; if transformation changed them, nonvirtue would become virtue, contradicting the natural course of cause and result. Yet if it were abandonment [of The Ground], that would conflict with the permanent essence and would not be mantra. Therefore it is a path of purification.
Vajra statement. Others say: “In mantra, practising nonvirtue with skillful means makes it virtue. Desire, hatred, stupidity, pride, and jealousy are not abandoned.”

Here nonvirtue prohibited in discipline is nonvirtue and something to abandon in mantra too; it does not become virtue. No one in the world, including its gods, can refute what buddhas’ primordial knowing of the possible and impossible sees and declares an obstacle to the path. Moreover, Vajradhara’s scrambling of continuums, twisting of transmissions, and concealment of instructions, and the six limits, chiefly involve statements with enlightened intent and nonliteral words, as well as concealed-meaning and general explanations among the four modes.[^N-B-081]

notes.problem: tshul bzhin can read appropriately; four modes would require tshul bzhi, suggested by the ensuing hermeneutic categories. The substring don spyi crosses the boundary between concealed meaning and general explanation; it is not meaning generalization here.
notes.treatment: Use among the four modes as an explicitly provisional interpretation. The lung bcus issue recurs from N-B-066.
notes.uncertainty: Spelling and category relation unresolved.
notes.review_action: Check witness and hermeneutic classification.

english: Thus the four samayas of Guhyasamaja’s four families, killing living beings and so forth, are explained in the Prediction of Enlightened Intent:

What is not given is the ordinary mind of awakening;
Teaching the relative is speaking falsely.
The aggregates are the living beings;
The four Brahma abodes are the women.
When explained through enlightened intent,
The childish understand “as they wish.”
Though wishing to abide in the “lord-lord vehicle,”
The nature of phenomena is its primordial knowing.[^N-B-082]

notes.problem: yi gar and rje rje are unusual and may conceal letters/literal interpretation and vajra vehicle.
notes.treatment: Retain literal as they wish and lord-lord vehicle in quotation marks.
notes.uncertainty: Probable textual defects; last two lines’ relationship uncertain.
notes.review_action: Check complete quotation and witness before reconstruction.

english: And:

Those confused about words of enlightened intent,
Not realizing the meaning of what is said,
Say, “It is nothing other than this statement,”
And then take the speech literally.
Thus acts connected with the three poisons are nonvirtuous even in mantra; without that connection, they are virtuous in mantra too.

Addendum. Others say that people of inferior, middling, and superior faculty train respectively with the three scriptural collections as The Ground and individual liberation, bodhisattva training, and so forth as paths, attaining three results: peaceful happiness, nonabiding nirvana, and union’s great bliss.

Here training in the vajra vehicle’s path stages requires all three, without removing or installing persons, teachings, results, and the rest as good or bad. They are the successive means, causes, and conditions for a single person to awaken, like a wise king’s establishing laws. The Two Examinations says, “First, confer restoration and purification,” and so forth.
Therefore the three trainings are certainly required universally as stages of the path throughout the vows, including mantra vows.

Addendum. Others say individual liberation, bodhisattva, and mantra are three distinct, different paths. Here the six perfections are the path of all three vehicles of sutra and mantra, because there is no way to awaken without relying on the two accumulations. The first three are the accumulation of merit, the last two the accumulation of primordial knowing, and diligence assists both. The glorious protector Nagarjuna’s Middle Way Precious Garland says:

In brief, these teachings of the Buddha
Consist solely of the six perfections.
This is known from that and other extensive teachings.

Vajra statement. Others say both the perfections and mantra explain afflictions as the buddhas’ ancestry and family. [Here] sugatahood is the result of purifying or becoming free from afflictions, since the impossibility of a path transforming The Ground has already been established. The Continuum of Kuntu Khwa says:[^N-B-083]

notes.problem: The reference is blank and the continuum title’s khwa is unusual.
notes.treatment: Transliterate Kuntu Khwa without identifying it as another known title.
notes.uncertainty: Title unresolved.
notes.review_action: Check witness and catalog identification.

english:
Through cultivating stupidity as perfectly pure,
One becomes Vairocana himself.
Through cultivating hatred as perfectly pure,
One becomes Akshobhya himself.

Through cultivating jealousy as perfectly pure,
One becomes Amoghasiddhi himself.
Through cultivating pride as perfectly pure,
One becomes Ratnasambhava himself.
And the great protector Drigungpa says:

The hero who determines the enemy as a friend
And the dakini who realizes the friend as empty—
The yogin whose ordinary mind is unchanging
Is “gor ro ro” without interruption.[^N-B-084]

notes.problem: The final gor ro ro is not securely parsed; the first line may describe turning an enemy into a friend or decisively recognizing one.
notes.treatment: Retain the final expression transliterated; use determines as a provisional first-line relation.
notes.uncertainty: Song wording and imagery uncertain.
notes.review_action: Identify the complete song and inspect witness.

english: The Cloud of Jewels says:

Liberator from the sorrow of existence,
Homage to you who liberated afflictions.
And:

When you abided at awakening’s heart,
Desire, hatred, stupidity,
And many other stains
Were burned by your fire of primordial knowing.

Through the path that purifies the three poisons, the result of separation arises: embodiments and primordial knowing, and an ocean of awakened deeds. Therefore they are called family and ancestry. Otherwise, without purifying afflictions themselves, they would not be ancestry even for higher destinies, much less for buddhas: they are ancestry for lower destinies.

Addendum. Others say channels, winds, and spheres, disrupted by the three poisons, are impure and must be purified. Although that accords with us, here channels, winds, and spheres with their dregs—“six” together—are profound.[^N-B-085] Pure embodiments and primordial knowing arise from a person whose channels and winds are impure. Without those three things to purify, a pure result could not arise, like a result without a cause. The Questions of Kashyapa says:

notes.problem: The source at U03113 reads dregs together with six, while U03110 has a disrupted phrase about stages and the three poisons.
notes.treatment: Retain six visibly and construe the three poisons as disrupting the three subtle-body factors.
notes.uncertainty: Exact grouping and whether drug should read dug, poison, remain uncertain.
notes.review_action: Check both readings against witness; do not normalize number to poison.

english:
As unclean manure from the city’s center
Benefits a field of sugarcane,
So the manure of bodhisattvas’ afflictions
Benefits the victors and the victors’ Dharma.

Accordingly, impure channels, winds, and spheres, like mire, serve as cause; relying on a holy guru’s instructions as condition and applying diligence brings attainment of purity. Although that impurity is present in all sentient beings, without complete conditions the result does not occur, just as gold ore left unworked does not yield gold.

Vajra statement. Others take literally the teaching that malicious beings must be liberated through mantra’s forceful ritual activity, and regard it as permitted because it is faultless. Here it merely displays mantra’s power or capacity; actual forceful activity is not permitted. Its application is hatred and conflicts with primordial knowing of what is possible and impossible and with the declaration of fearlessness. The Manjushri Root Continuum says:

King Chandra appointed the brahmin Chanakya, a yogin of the Lord of Death, as his officiating guru. Because he killed many enemies through forceful ritual activity, he took that deity’s form and was born in hell. Given that account, what need to say that killing through reliance on Tsangtsen, Pehar, and the like leads to birth in lower destinies?

Was it not permitted, then? It is the deed of someone able to revive those killed, transfer consciousness, and realize all phenomena as evenness—someone like Lord Jowo, Jetsun Mila, or master Padma. The Continuum of the Lord of Death’s Fire Peak says:

Except for liberating afflictions
Through the compassionate responsiveness of clear self-awareness,
“Liberation” with an ordinary mind of hatred and malice
Brings birth in the hell of Unceasing Torment.
So it says.

Vajra statement. Others say vajra hell is a place apart from the eighteen hells explained in the causal vehicle, with especially great suffering. Here it has no separate location: it is those eighteen, Unceasing Torment and the rest. The Realization of the Unmoving One and Fifty Verses on the Guru say:

Whatever terrifying hells are taught,
Unceasing Torment and the rest—
Those who disparage their masters
Are taught to abide there certainly.
The Vajra Pavilion says:

If a disciple who has then attained
Supreme empowerment transgresses the guru’s word,
They suffer in this world
And afterward abide in Unceasing Torment.
Secret mantra also identifies Wailing as the vajra hell, Unceasing Torment.[^N-B-086] The Stainless Light commentary on Kalachakra says:

notes.problem: Wailing, vajra hell, and Unceasing Torment are compressed into one classification.
notes.treatment: Retain the identification provisionally rather than invent a separate location.
notes.uncertainty: Exact equivalence and case attachment uncertain.
notes.review_action: Compare the Kalachakra classification and source witness.

english: Wailing is in the center of the wind mandala, and Great Darkness above it. Likewise the fire mandala contains Fire Hell and Unbearable Wailing; the water mandala contains Muddy Water and Sandy Water; and the lower half of the earth mandala contains Gravel Hell. These seven places are said to encompass the hot and cold hells with their surroundings.

Vajra statement. Although others say that one who transgresses samaya and is born in vajra hell will never attain liberation, here a master with a highly developed continuum will swiftly lead that person out. [The assertion of endless confinement] is an exhortation based on Dharma. For example, Youth Difficult to Subdue taught Tharpa Nakpo:

If that suchness is uncontrived,
Even abiding in the four great [offenses],
Like clouds in space …[^N-B-087]

notes.problem: The quote ends mid-comparison and gives four great without naming what is counted.
notes.treatment: Supply offenses in brackets from the ensuing literalist misconduct narrative; keep the comparison incomplete.
notes.uncertainty: Fourfold referent requires confirmation.
notes.review_action: Verify narrative and full quotation.

english: Taking that and similar teachings literally, [Tharpa Nakpo] performed inexhaustible karma and fell into lower destinies. Dedpak manifested as the Great Terrifier and led him out.[^N-B-088]

notes.problem: mi zad literally says inexhaustible, although dreadful actions would fit the narrative; Dedpak’s identity is not documented here.
notes.treatment: Retain inexhaustible karma and transliterate Dedpak rather than supplying an unverified Sanskrit identification.
notes.uncertainty: Possible spelling defect and narrative-name ambiguity.
notes.review_action: Check witness and the Tharpa Nakpo account.

english: Addendum. Others say: “When a disciple despises the master, the first root downfall of mantra is incurred, so a disciple’s samaya is extremely exacting; the master’s obligation toward the disciple is not comparably exacting.”

Here master and disciple are equal in how exacting their mutual samaya is. A master who despises a disciple incurs the twelfth root downfall; and when someone commits a fault, even a guru, its result arises through dependent arising. [Source marker: ས།][^N-B-089] Just as either a mother who kills her child or a child who kills their mother falls into hell.

notes.problem: An isolated sa followed by shad precedes the clause about consequences.
notes.treatment: Keep it visibly as an unresolved source marker.
notes.uncertainty: Could be a stray syllable or a marker; no evidential basis for deletion.

english: This is the fifth section: the explanation of twenty-eight vajra statements and seventeen supplementary statements, gathering the essential points of secret mantra.
